name: Curve pETH/ETH Vyper lock reentrancy
summary: Vyper 0.2.15 allocated the same named nonreentrant lock to different storage slots in different functions. The pETH/ETH pool's native-ETH callback therefore allowed cross-function reentrancy from remove_liquidity() into add_liquidity(), minting an invalid claim on pool reserves.
notes: Curve's factory deployed an immutable 45-byte EIP-1167 clone whose runtime embeds implementation 0x6326debbaa15bcfe603d831e7d75f4fc10d9b43e. Both clone and implementation runtimes remained unchanged through the exploit.

The exploit receipt records exactly 86,106.654659206663837483 WETH wrapped after the pool operations, 80,000 WETH repaid to Balancer, and 6,106.654659206663837483 WETH transferred as net proceeds. Later recovery is separate from exploit-time loss. Other Vyper-affected pools were attacked independently and are not included.
